tools.name: Blender
tools.note: DECLARED entry — payload staging is the remaining packaging step: take the official Blender release archive per platform, repack it as the library zip named below, split it with planParts(size, PART_BYTES), SHA-256 every part and the whole, fill size/sha256/parts in, and flip payloadStatus to 'staged'. The version is series-level (4.5 LTS) until staging pins the exact upstream point release. Until then the pull path refuses this tool and Blender steps stay declared — nothing is faked. Blender is GPL-3.0, so the binaries are redistributable through the library. The Blender MCP bridge in catalog/extensions.json is the companion surface; this item is the engine itself.

quality.basis: Blender is the fleet's render engine of record — the render methods and the Blender Lab MCP bridge (catalog/extensions.json) already target it; GPL-3.0 makes the binaries redistributable.

tools.name: Langcheck — parse checkers for translated code
tools.note: DECLARED entry — the checker bundle for the code translator (catalog/methods/code-translate.method.md; design 2026-11-14, section 3.2): one small Node dispatcher named langcheck that maps a file's extension to that language's own parse checker — node --check for JavaScript, node:module type-stripping plus node --check for TypeScript, python3 -m py_compile for Python, bash -n for Bash — and prints its verdict on stdout (langcheck: OK <language> (checker: <name>) / FAIL / NO-CHECKER when the language has no checker in the bundle or the checker binary is absent on the node). Exit 0 means the file parses (or no checker covers it — the NO-CHECKER line says which, and callers never grade that as a parse pass); exit 1 means the checker ran and the file does not parse. The bundle is BUILT: langcheck 1.0.0 was packaged (zip, planParts parts, SHA-256 pins) in the translator build's staging manifest and proven end to end against a locally staged copy on 2026-11-14 (pulled, hash-verified, materialized, executed by the conductor's declare path). Payload staging into the library payload store is the remaining seat act: place the parts per the staging manifest, fill size/sha256/parts from it, and flip payloadStatus to 'staged'. Until then the pull path refuses this tool and parse-check steps stay declared — translation grades stay STRUCT or NONE, nothing is faked. First-party bundle, written by the fleet for the Brain Library; the license label is catalog bookkeeping and redistribution terms are the owner's call.

quality.basis: Built for the code translator's verification lane: deterministic parse verdicts from the languages' own checkers, executed only through the conductor's library-pulled declare path (a PATH binary never executes). Proven against a locally staged copy in the translator build's proof run (2026-11-14); staged in no payload store yet.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.note: STAGED 2026-11-14 (linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos-arm64, windows-x64) from the official OpenCode v1.19.5 upstream CLI release assets (github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.19.5, published 2026-10-28). Every download was verified against the digest in the vendor's own release record before repack: opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz sha256 588310a336fa3b9df36b3f0225b26f679d453efaad0cf3d66c3651ef3ec1647a, opencode-linux-arm64.tar.gz sha256 fae5be262d693b7c5e562856cc473e59e741772936db0c0600ac0d5ed5bd088b, opencode-darwin-arm64.zip sha256 c1c9e62521192192ef4c3ed1355ada2144055bddb61682217e997b03c55203c1, opencode-windows-x64.zip sha256 09a6e693157f0887e504f2cf4357a8cbddc5ead5d0dffb9a269dcc47c48640f5. Only the CLI assets are carried — the desktop app builds are not the tool the conductor runs. REPACK LAYOUT: none needed — each upstream archive carries exactly one bare binary at its root (opencode / opencode.exe), which is where the catalog's bin fields point; the library zips hold that binary byte-preserved (each binary's SHA-256 re-verified inside the finished zip) plus the upstream LICENSE (MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 opencode — read from the v1.19.5 tag). Each zip is under PART_BYTES (1,900,000,000), so planParts yields exactly one part per platform (.part-aa, byte-identical to the zip). Upstream also ships baseline (pre-AVX2) and musl variants; the platform key carries one payload, so the primary glibc builds are staged — stage a baseline variant under the same key if a pre-AVX2 node joins. MACOS-X64 and WINDOWS-ARM64 are DECLARED-NOT-STAGED: the vendor assets exist (opencode-darwin-x64.zip, opencode-windows-arm64.zip) and the identical repack stages them on demand. Payloads are staged LOCALLY (opencode-brain-library-2026-11-14/payload/) until the owner uploads the parts to ronininc/weights releases tagged opencode-1.19.5-<platform> and the landed assets verify against these pins. Conducted via catalog/methods/opencode-code-task.method.md (headless `opencode run`).

quality.basis: The fleet's designated local coding harness (MIT, anomalyco/opencode). Pinned to the vendor's current release v1.19.5 with every staged payload digest-verified against the vendor's own release record and the binary bytes re-verified inside the repack; the wiring build (2026-11-14) ran the staged linux-x64 binary headless on a real code task through the method conductor and kept the receipts.

why: Tools — the engine layer of the Brain Library (tool streaming, 2026-11-11). Training modules teach Kingmaker how to reason, method files script what to do, models stream as weights — and tool items carry the engines a method step invokes: one release archive per platform, split into hashed parts (planParts, the model-weights machinery), the whole archive SHA-256-pinned. A node missing the binary pulls the tool through lib/brain-library-access.mjs, materializes it via lib/brain-library-fetch.mjs, registers it with the tool-calling layer, and the method conductor executes the step instead of declaring it skipped. A platform whose payloadStatus is 'declared-not-staged' declares the part-layout contract only: no hashes exist yet, and every pull path refuses it (fail closed) until the packaging step stages the real payload.
